Judge-scored accuracy corrected with human labels

Source: R/core-bench-judge.R
hr_judge_ppi.Rd

A judge's accuracy figures are biased by its own errors. Given the judge's score on every item and human labels on a sample of them, this returns the prediction-powered estimate of the human-scored mean (Angelopoulos et al. 2023), through hr_ppi():

Usage

hr_judge_ppi(
  judge_scores,
  human_labels,
  inclusion_prob = NULL,
  conf = 0.95,
  tune = TRUE
)

Arguments

judge_scores

The judge's score for every item, numeric or logical (1 or TRUE for right), no NA.

human_labels

The human score on the same scale, the same length, NA on the items no person labelled.

inclusion_prob

NULL, or the probability with which each item was chosen for human labelling: one per item, or one per labelled item.

conf

Confidence level.

tune

Whether to tune lambda (PPI++); see hr_ppi().

Value

The one-row data frame of hr_ppi(), with judge_mean, the uncorrected mean of judge_scores, added.

Details

estimate = mean(judge on unlabelled) + mean(human - judge on labelled)

with PPI++ tuning by default. When inclusion_prob varies, the labelled items were drawn with unequal probabilities and the correction is inverse-probability weighted, the design-based supervised learning form (Egami et al. 2023):

estimate = mean over all items of
           lambda * judge_i + R_i * (human_i - lambda * judge_i) / pi_i

with R_i = 1 for labelled items. Equal probabilities give the plain form.

The interval is a normal approximation and needs enough labelled items in every inclusion stratum. Small inclusion probabilities with few labels give intervals that are too narrow: with about 150 labels drawn at 0.05 and 0.4, a nominal 95% interval covered the true mean about 91% of the time in simulation.

References

Angelopoulos, A. N., Bates, S., Fannjiang, C., Jordan, M. I. and Zrnic, T. (2023). Prediction-powered inference. Science 382(6671), 669-674.

Egami, N., Hinck, M., Stewart, B. M. and Wei, H. (2023). Using imperfect surrogates for downstream inference: design-based supervised learning for social science applications of large language models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36.

See also

hr_ppi(), hr_judge_validate()

Other judges: hr_judge(), hr_judge_config(), hr_judge_validate(), hr_scorer_judge()

Examples

set.seed(7)
truth <- rbinom(1000, 1, 0.6)
# A lenient judge: it passes 30% of wrong answers.
judge <- ifelse(truth == 1, rbinom(1000, 1, 0.95), rbinom(1000, 1, 0.3))
human <- rep(NA, 1000)
lab <- sample(1000, 150)
human[lab] <- truth[lab]
hr_judge_ppi(judge, human)
#>    estimate         se     lower     upper   n   N    lambda method judge_mean
#> 1 0.5668593 0.03135783 0.5053991 0.6283196 150 850 0.6349485  ppi++      0.698
